newsitem.title: UK: UK court allows landmark tobacco case to proceed.
newsitem.headline: UK court allows landmark tobacco case to proceed.

text.p: A British court agreed to allow the country's first case in which lung cancer victims will try to claim compensation from tobacco companies to proceed, a lawyer for the plaintiffs said on Friday.

The High Court named a judge for the preliminary stages of the case which could result in multi-billion pound (dollar) payments against Imperial Tobacco Group Plc and Gallaher Group Plc if the 47 plaintiffs are successful.
"I'm delighted they've agreed to go ahead and that they've allocated a judge to deal with it speedily," said Martyn Day, the plaintiffs' lawyer, after he received the ruling.
The group action is Europe's largest ever legal battle against the tobacco industry and legal experts say it could open a floodgate of similar law suits.
The decision, which followed a private hearing, also considered whether each side had the right documents and how long the court case might last.

Day claims the companies, which own brands such as Benson and Hedges, Silk Cut and Embassy and control 80 percent of the British cigarette market, were aware in the 1950s that their products were addictive and killing large numbers of people. The tobacco companies say there is no proof that by reducing the tar levels in cigarettes smokers would not have suffered from cancer.
